c1-oba-0001: Obadiah brings a warning to Edom about those who will turn against it. Let's read Obadiah 1:7 together.
c2-oba-0001: Obadiah lists what Edom should not have done in Judah's day of distress. Let's read Obadiah 1:12 and 1:14.
c2-num-0011: Edom's king refused Israel passage and threatened to come out against them. Let's read Numbers 20:17 and 20:19.
c3-num-0005: Edom would not let Israel pass through his territory. Let's read Numbers 20:20-21.
c3-oba-0001: Obadiah says Edom will be made small among the nations. Let's read Obadiah 1:2 and 1:11.
c3-oba-0002: The LORD says He will destroy the wise men from Edom. Let's read Obadiah 1:8 and 1:17.
c3-oba-0003: Obadiah condemns Edom for violence against its brother Jacob. Let's read Obadiah 1:10 and 1:18.
c3-gen-0012: The LORD told Rebekah that two nations were in her womb. Let's read Genesis 25:23 and 36:33.
c1-nah-0001: Amid warnings of judgment on Nineveh, Nahum pauses to speak of the LORD's goodness. Let's read Nahum 1:7 together.
c2-nah-0001: Nahum promises Judah that the LORD will break the yoke off them. Let's read Nahum 1:13 and 1:15.
c2-nah-0002: Nahum compares Nineveh with another great city that had waters around her. Let's read Nahum 3:8-9.
c3-jon-0001: God saw that Nineveh turned from its evil way, and He relented. Let's read Jonah 3:6 and 3:10.
c3-nah-0001: Nahum says that with an overflowing flood the LORD will make an utter end of Nineveh's place. Let's read Nahum 1:8 and 2:6.
c3-nah-0002: Nahum says affliction will not rise up a second time. Let's read Nahum 1:9 and 3:19.
c3-nah-0003: Nahum mocks Nineveh about manning the fort and watching the road. Let's read Nahum 2:1 and 3:14.
c3-jon-0002: God relented from the disaster He had said He would bring on Nineveh. Let's read Jonah 3:10 and 4:11.
c1-zep-0001: Zephaniah announces judgment on Judah for mixed worship. Let's read Zephaniah 1:5.
c2-zep-0001: The LORD will search Jerusalem closely and punish certain men there. Let's read Zephaniah 1:12-13.
c2-zep-0002: Zephaniah calls the humble of the land to seek the LORD, righteousness, and humility. Let's read Zephaniah 2:2-3.
c3-zep-0001: Zephaniah says Jerusalem's priests have polluted the sanctuary. Let's read Zephaniah 3:3-4.
c3-zep-0002: Zephaniah condemns those who have turned back from following the LORD. Let's read Zephaniah 1:6 and 3:17.
c3-zep-0003: The LORD tells the faithful to wait for Him. Let's read Zephaniah 2:1 and 3:8.
c3-zep-0004: Zephaniah pronounces woe on the oppressing city. Let's read Zephaniah 2:15 and 3:1.
c3-zep-0005: The LORD stretches out His hand against Judah, and later against the north. Let's read Zephaniah 1:4 and 2:14.
c1-phm-0001: Paul addresses Philemon, and he names others as well. Let's read Philemon 1:2.
c2-phm-0001: Paul thanks God for Philemon whenever he prays. Let's read Philemon 1:4-5.
c2-col-0004: Paul tells the Colossians that Tychicus is coming with Onesimus. Let's read Colossians 4:7 and 4:9.
c3-phm-0001: Paul says he might be bold enough to command Philemon, yet he chooses another way. Let's read Philemon 1:8 and 1:14.
c3-phm-0002: Paul prays that the sharing of Philemon's faith may become effective. Let's read Philemon 1:6 and 1:21.
c3-phm-0003: Paul suggests Onesimus departed for a while so Philemon might receive him forever. Let's read Philemon 1:15 and 1:18.
c3-phm-0004: Paul calls himself a prisoner of Christ Jesus. Let's read Philemon 1:1 and 1:13.
c3-phm-0005: Paul often remembered Philemon with thanks, and later he sent Onesimus back. Let's read Philemon 1:4 and 1:12.
c1-2jn-0001: The Elder writes to the elect lady with great joy. Let's read Second John 1:4.
c2-2jn-0001: The Elder reminds the lady that what he writes is nothing new. Let's read Second John 1:2 and 1:6.
c2-2jn-0002: The Elder writes about a visitor who does not bring the doctrine of Christ. Let's read Second John 1:10-11.
c3-2jn-0001: The Elder tells readers to look to themselves, so they do not lose what was worked for. Let's read Second John 1:8 and 1:11.
c3-2jn-0002: The Elder contrasts those who abide in the doctrine of Christ with those who do not. Let's read Second John 1:3 and 1:9.
c3-2jn-0003: The elect sister's household sends greetings at the close of the letter. Let's read Second John 1:13 and 1:7.
c1-3jn-0001: The Elder wrote, but one man would not receive him. Let's read Third John 1:9.
c2-3jn-0001: The Elder says we ought to receive such workers. Let's read Third John 1:8 and 1:10.
c2-3jn-0002: Gaius has been faithful to brethren and to strangers. Let's read Third John 1:5-6.
c3-3jn-0001: The Elder commends a man of whom everyone speaks well, and he adds his own witness. Let's read Third John 1:11-12.
c3-3jn-0002: The Elder writes of his greatest joy when he hears good news about those he loves. Let's read Third John 1:4 and 1:7.
c3-3jn-0003: The Elder tells Gaius he has many things still to write. Let's read Third John 1:11 and 1:13.
c2-exo-0022: At Sinai the LORD sent Moses to tell Israel what they would be if they kept His covenant. Let's read Exodus 19:6.
c2-2sa-0009: God promises that David's offspring shall be His son. Let's read Second Samuel 7:14-15.
c3-jer-0013: The LORD says the coming covenant will not be like the one made when He led their fathers from Egypt. Let's read Jeremiah 31:32 and 31:34.
c3-heb-0009: Hebrews explains why a second covenant was needed, and then it turns to Jeremiah's promise. Let's read Hebrews 8:7-8.
c3-2sa-0009: God reminds David that He has been with him and has cut off those who opposed him. Let's read Second Samuel 7:9-10.
c3-gen-0013: The LORD made a covenant with Abram about the land, after an earlier covenant with Noah. Let's read Genesis 9:12 and 15:18.
c3-gen-0014: God says the waters shall never again become a flood. Let's read Genesis 9:15 and 17:4.
c3-gen-0015: The LORD appeared to Abram and called him to walk before Him. Let's read Genesis 15:7 and 17:1.
c3-gen-0016: As Abram waited beside the divided sacrifice, something happened. Let's read Genesis 9:10 and 15:11.
c3-gen-0017: Abram asked how he would know that he would inherit the land. Let's read Genesis 15:8 and 17:2.
